items.title: Rise of the INC & the Moderate Phase (1885-1905)
items.body:
## Before the Congress

- Middle-class discontent first found voice in regional associations: **Landholders' Society (1837)**, **British Indian Association (1851)**, **Indian National Association (S.N. Banerjee, 1876)**, **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870)** and **Madras Mahajan Sabha (1884)**. Several merged into the Congress after 1885.

## Founding of the INC

- Founded **December 1885** at **Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay** through **A.O. Hume**; first president **W.C. Bonnerjee**; **72 delegates**.
- The **Safety Valve theory** holds that Hume intended the Congress to release Indian discontent peacefully.

## The Moderates

- Leaders: **Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Surendranath Banerjee, Pherozeshah Mehta**.
- **Methods**: petitions, resolutions, speeches, delegations — 'constitutional agitation' (dubbed *Political Mendicancy*).
- **Demands**: Indianisation of services, reduced military spending, council representation, civil rights — but **self-government within the Empire**, not independence.
- **Drain of Wealth theory** (Naoroji, *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*, 1901) exposed economic exploitation.

| 'First' | Person | Session |
|---|---|---|
| First president | W.C. Bonnerjee | 1885 |
| First Muslim president | Badruddin Tyabji | 1887 |
| First woman president | Annie Besant | 1917 |
| First Indian woman president | Sarojini Naidu | 1925 |
keyPoints: INC founded December 1885 at Bombay by A.O. Hume; first president W.C. Bonnerjee; 72 delegates.
The Safety Valve theory: Hume meant the Congress to defuse Indian discontent peacefully.
Moderate leaders: Naoroji, Gokhale, Surendranath Banerjee, Pherozeshah Mehta; methods were petitions and resolutions.
Moderates sought self-government within the Empire, not full independence.
Dadabhai Naoroji's Drain of Wealth theory appears in Poverty and Un-British Rule in India (1901).
Badruddin Tyabji = first Muslim president (1887); Annie Besant = first woman president (1917); Sarojini Naidu = first Indian woman president (1925).
items.mnemonic: Moderate quartet 'NGBM' = Naoroji, Gokhale, Banerjee, Mehta.

items.title: Extremist Phase, Swadeshi & Revolutionaries (1905-1917)
items.body:
## Partition of Bengal & Swadeshi

- **Lord Curzon** partitioned **Bengal (1905)** into a Muslim-majority east and Hindu-majority west, sparking the **Swadeshi and Boycott Movement** (boycott of British goods, promotion of khadi and national schools). Partition **annulled in 1911**.

## The Extremists

- **Lal-Bal-Pal** — **Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal** — plus **Aurobindo Ghose**.
- Tilak: *'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'*; wrote *Gita Rahasya*; promoted Ganpati and Shivaji festivals.
- **Surat Split (1907)**: Congress divided into Moderates and Extremists; reunited at **Lucknow (1916)**.

## Revolutionary Nationalism

- **Anushilan Samiti** and **Jugantar** in Bengal; **Aurobindo's *Bande Mataram*** and the **Alipore Bomb Case (1908-09)**; **Khudiram Bose** hanged (1908).
- **Ghadar Party (1913, USA)** — Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, Rashbehari Bose — planned armed revolt during WWI.
- Later, the **HSRA** (Bhagat Singh, Chandrasekhar Azad, Sukhdev, Rajguru); Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru executed **1931**.

## Constitutional context

- **Muslim League founded (1906, Dhaka)**; **Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)** introduced **separate electorates**.
- **Home Rule Movement (1916)** — Tilak (Maharashtra) and Annie Besant (Madras).
keyPoints: Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905 (annulled 1911), triggering the Swadeshi/Boycott Movement.
Lal-Bal-Pal = Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal; Tilak coined 'Swaraj is my birthright'.
Surat Split (1907) divided Congress into Moderates and Extremists; they reunited at Lucknow (1916).
Aurobindo Ghose ran Bande Mataram and was tried in the Alipore Bomb Case (1908-09).
Ghadar Party (1913, USA) led by Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna and Rashbehari Bose.
Muslim League founded 1906 at Dhaka; Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) introduced separate electorates.
Home Rule Leagues (1916) run by Tilak (Maharashtra) and Annie Besant (Madras).
items.mnemonic: 'Lal-Bal-Pal' = Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, (Bipin Chandra) Pal.

items.title: Mass Movements: 1919-1934
items.body:
## Rowlatt & Jallianwala Bagh (1919)

- The **Rowlatt Act** allowed detention without trial; protests culminated in the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919, Amritsar)** under **General Dyer**. Tagore renounced his knighthood.

## Non-Cooperation & Khilafat (1920-22)

- Gandhi's **Non-Cooperation Movement** merged with the **Khilafat Movement** (Ali Brothers) for Hindu-Muslim unity: boycott of schools, courts, titles and foreign goods.
- Withdrawn after the **Chauri Chaura incident (Feb 1922)**.

## Swaraj Party (1923)

- **C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru** formed the Swaraj Party to enter legislative councils and obstruct from within.

## Towards Civil Disobedience

- **Simon Commission (1927)** — all-British; 'Simon, go back'; Lajpat Rai fatally injured.
- **Nehru Report (1928)** — Motilal Nehru; demanded Dominion Status.
- **Civil Disobedience Movement (1930)** began with the **Dandi Salt March**; **Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)**; **Round Table Conferences (1930-32)**; **Communal Award (1932)** and **Poona Pact (1932)**.

| Event | Year |
|---|---|
| Rowlatt Act / Jallianwala Bagh | 1919 |
| Non-Cooperation / Khilafat | 1920-22 |
| Chauri Chaura | 1922 |
| Dandi March / CDM | 1930 |
| Gandhi-Irwin Pact | 1931 |
| GoI Act | 1935 |
keyPoints: Rowlatt Act (1919) allowed detention without trial; Jallianwala Bagh massacre 13 April 1919 under General Dyer.
Non-Cooperation (1920-22) merged with the Khilafat Movement; withdrawn after Chauri Chaura (1922).
Swaraj Party (1923) founded by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru for council entry.
Simon Commission (1927) was all-British; met with 'Simon, go back'; Lajpat Rai fatally injured.
Nehru Report (1928), chaired by Motilal Nehru, demanded Dominion Status.
Civil Disobedience began with the Dandi March (1930); Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931; GoI Act 1935 gave provincial autonomy.

items.title: From Purna Swaraj to Independence (1929-1947)
items.body:
## Purna Swaraj (1929)

- **Lahore Session (1929)**, president **Jawaharlal Nehru**, adopted the **Purna Swaraj** resolution; **26 January 1930** observed as the first Independence Day.

## The 1935 Act & Provincial Rule

- The **Government of India Act, 1935** introduced **provincial autonomy** and a federal scheme; Congress won the **1937 provincial elections** and formed ministries, which **resigned in 1939** over India's unilateral entry into WWII.

## Quit India (1942)

- Launched **8 August 1942**, Bombay, with **'Do or Die'**. Leaders were jailed; underground work by **Aruna Asaf Ali, Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, Sucheta Kripalani**.

## The Road to 1947

| Step | Year | Feature |
|---|---|---|
| August Offer | 1940 | Dominion status offer; rejected |
| Cripps Mission | 1942 | Post-war Dominion status; rejected |
| Cabinet Mission | 1946 | Federal union, province grouping |
| Direct Action Day | 1946 | League's call; Calcutta riots |
| RIN Mutiny | 1946 | Naval ratings' revolt, Bombay |
| Mountbatten Plan | 1947 | Partition; freedom by 15 Aug 1947 |
| Indian Independence Act | 1947 | Created India and Pakistan |
keyPoints: Lahore Session (1929, Nehru) adopted Purna Swaraj; 26 January 1930 was the first Independence Day.
GoI Act 1935 gave provincial autonomy; Congress won 1937 elections and formed ministries, resigning in 1939.
Quit India launched 8 August 1942 with 'Do or Die'; underground leaders included Aruna Asaf Ali and JP Narayan.
Cripps Mission (1942) and Cabinet Mission (1946) both failed to prevent partition.
Direct Action Day (1946) led to Calcutta riots; the RIN Mutiny (1946) shook the Raj.
Mountbatten Plan (1947) recommended Partition; the Indian Independence Act (July 1947) created India and Pakistan.
items.mnemonic: Road to 1947 'August-Cripps-Cabinet-Mountbatten' = the four big offers/plans in order.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Modern History: Freedom Movement (1930-1939); (1939-1947)

items.title: Subhas Chandra Bose, the Forward Bloc & the INA
items.body:
## Bose & the Congress

- **Subhas Chandra Bose** was elected Congress President at **Haripura (1938)** and again at **Tripuri (1939)**, but **resigned in 1939** after conflict with the Working Committee and Gandhi over methods.
- He founded the **Forward Bloc (1939)** to unite the radical left within the Congress.

## The INA

- Bose escaped to Germany and then Japan; he **reorganised the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj)** from Indian POWs, with the **Rani of Jhansi women's regiment**.
- Slogans: **'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom'** and **'Jai Hind'**.
- The INA campaigned in north-east India; though defeated, the **INA Trials (1945-46)** at the Red Fort roused huge public sympathy and pressured the British.
keyPoints: Bose was Congress President at Haripura (1938) and Tripuri (1939); resigned in 1939.
He founded the Forward Bloc (1939) to rally the Congress left.
Bose reorganised the INA (Azad Hind Fauj) with Japanese support, including the Rani of Jhansi regiment.
Slogans: 'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom' and 'Jai Hind'.
The INA Trials (1945-46) at the Red Fort generated mass nationalist sentiment.

items.title: Peasant & Tribal Movements (with AP angle)
items.body:
## Peasant Movements

| Movement | Region | Leader/Note |
|---|---|---|
| Indigo Revolt (1859-60) | Bengal | Biswas brothers; *Neel Darpan* |
| Deccan Riots (1875) | Maharashtra | against sahukars; Relief Act 1879 |
| Pabna Movement (1873-85) | Bengal | Ishan Chandra Roy; agrarian league |
| Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) | Gujarat | Vallabhbhai Patel ('Sardar') |
| All India Kisan Sabha (1936) | national | Swami Sahajanand Saraswati |
| Tebhaga (1946) | Bengal | sharecroppers; two-thirds share |
| Telangana (1946-52) | Andhra/Telangana | against Nizam's jagirdars; CPI-led |

## Tribal Revolts

- Mainland: **Santhal Rebellion (1855-56, Sidhu & Kanhu)**, **Kol Mutiny (1831)**, **Munda Ulgulan (Birsa Munda, 1899-1900)**.
- **Andhra**: **Koya Revolts** (Godavari), **Khond Uprisings** (Srikakulam/Visakhapatnam, Chakra Bisoi), and **Alluri Sitarama Raju's Rampa Rebellion (1922-24)** against colonial forest laws.

## Political currents in the struggle

- Beyond the Congress: the **Muslim League** (separate-electorate/two-nation politics), the **Communist Party of India** (peasant/worker mobilisation, e.g. Tebhaga, Telangana), and the **Justice/Liberal parties**.
keyPoints: Indigo Revolt (1859-60, Bengal) inspired the play Neel Darpan; Deccan Riots (1875) led to the 1879 Relief Act.
Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) under Vallabhbhai Patel earned him the title 'Sardar'.
All India Kisan Sabha (1936) founded by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati demanded abolition of zamindari.
Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) led by Sidhu and Kanhu; Munda Ulgulan led by Birsa Munda.
In Andhra, the Koya and Khond revolts and Alluri Sitarama Raju's Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) resisted colonial forest laws.
Non-Congress political currents: Muslim League, Communist Party of India, and the Justice/Liberal parties.

items.title: Key INC Sessions at a Glance
items.body:
## Landmark sessions

| Year | Place | President | Landmark |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1885 | Bombay | W.C. Bonnerjee | First session; 72 delegates |
| 1906 | Calcutta | Dadabhai Naoroji | First mention of 'Swaraj' |
| 1907 | Surat | Rash Behari Ghosh | Surat Split |
| 1916 | Lucknow | A.C. Mazumdar | Lucknow Pact; Moderate-Extremist reunion |
| 1920 | Nagpur | C. Vijayaraghavachariar | Ratified Non-Cooperation; CWC set up |
| 1924 | Belgaum | M.K. Gandhi | Only session Gandhi presided |
| 1929 | Lahore | Jawaharlal Nehru | Purna Swaraj resolution |
| 1931 | Karachi | Vallabhbhai Patel | Fundamental Rights; condemned Bhagat Singh's execution |
| 1938 | Haripura | Subhas Chandra Bose | National Planning Committee |
| 1939 | Tripuri | Subhas Chandra Bose | Bose resigned; Forward Bloc |

- Note: **'Vande Mataram'** first sung at **Calcutta (1896)**; **'Jana Gana Mana'** first sung at **Calcutta (1911)**.
keyPoints: Calcutta 1906 (Naoroji) saw the first official mention of 'Swaraj'.
Nagpur 1920 ratified Non-Cooperation and set up the Congress Working Committee.
Belgaum 1924 was the only session Gandhi personally presided over.
Karachi 1931 (Patel) adopted the Fundamental Rights resolution and condemned Bhagat Singh's execution.
Haripura (1938) and Tripuri (1939) were Bose's two presidencies.
'Vande Mataram' first sung at Calcutta (1896); 'Jana Gana Mana' first sung at Calcutta (1911).

items.title: Swadeshi Institutions, Surat Split & Ghadar (PYQ set)
items.body:
## Swadeshi Movement (1905) — the constructive side

- 'Swadeshi' and 'Boycott' were **first adopted during the anti-Partition (of Bengal) agitation, 1905**.
- It **revived indigenous crafts and industries** (khadi, indigenous soap, matches, textiles) and built **national education**: the **National Council of Education (NCE) was set up in 1906**, founding the **Bengal National College** (Aurobindo Ghose its first principal).

## Why the Surat Split (1907) happened

- The Congress split at Surat mainly because the **Extremists lost faith in the Moderates' capacity to negotiate** meaningful reform through petitions; disputes over the presidency and over passing Swadeshi/boycott resolutions triggered the break. The two wings **reunited at Lucknow (1916)**.

## Ghadar Party (1913)

- A **revolutionary association of Indians (mainly Punjabi emigrants) with headquarters at San Francisco (USA)**, founded 1913; leaders **Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha**; **Rash Behari Bose** was closely associated. It planned an armed revolt during WWI (the failed Ghadar conspiracy of 1915).

## Lucknow Pact (1916)

- Congress–Muslim League agreement (Tilak & Jinnah): Congress **accepted separate electorates**; joint demand for self-government.
keyPoints: Swadeshi/Boycott were first adopted in the 1905 anti-Partition (of Bengal) agitation.
The Swadeshi Movement revived indigenous crafts AND set up the National Council of Education (1906) / Bengal National College (Aurobindo first principal).
Surat Split (1907): Extremists lost faith in the Moderates' capacity to negotiate; reunion at Lucknow (1916).
Ghadar Party (1913) — revolutionary Indians with HQ at San Francisco; Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha, Rash Behari Bose.
Lucknow Pact (1916): Congress-League unity, Congress accepted separate electorates (Tilak-Jinnah).
items.mnemonic: Swadeshi 1905 builds NCE 1906 → Surat splits 1907 → Lucknow reunites 1916.
